_readme: Committed p95 latency budgets for the nightly-load-test CI job (#1082). See docs/development/nightly-load-test.md for the full contract: fixture size, budget-derivation rule, and how to re-derive this file at each release. DO NOT hand-edit budget_p95_ms to a round number — every value here must trace to a measured_p95_ms via the stated formula.
status_note: Re-derived 2026-10-21 (#1808) from job 17348200339, pipeline 2971900609 -- a manual run of the nightly-load-test schedule on main at 58a4299b5 on gitlab-runner-nuc-2-visiban (tag nuc), the first NUC run that includes the #1800 timestamptz backport, the #1805 literal-board-id card filter and the #1810 card_search_multi_board scenario with its 199 extra boards. Values below are that run's measured p95/p99 per endpoint, unchanged from the artifact, with budget_p95_ms recomputed via the formula for the whole file in one pass; card_search_multi_board gains its first budget and its pending_budget key is gone. This is a single run: board_full measured 1227.5ms against 1210.5ms in the previous derivation (job 17304593759 on runner-04-NUC), so the #1800 backport did not lower it on this sample and its budget rose from 1695 to 1720ms; the other budgets fell. The two derivations ran on different runners, so the changes are not a clean before/after of the code. History: 2026-10-20 (#1767) from job 17304593759, pipeline 2965970261, on runner-04-NUC; 2026-09-30 (#1233) from job 16796708105 on gitlab-runner-nuc-2-visiban. Re-derive again at the next release per the procedure in docs/development/nightly-load-test.md#re-deriving-the-baseline.

fixture.note: --scale 20 replicates the 10-swimlane demo layout 20x (11-13 cards/swimlane, same distribution as the normal demo board) rather than picking an arbitrary target card count directly. The load-test board has 20 members (5 demo users + 15 loadtest* filler accounts, #1723).
fixture.multi_board_note: #1810: --extra-boards 199 adds 199 small boards (8 cards each, 1,592 cards) owned by demo3, so demo3 can access 200 boards with the load-test board. The extra boards belong to demo3 alone, so the demo1 board_list and demo2 scenarios see the same boards as before. Every measured_p95_ms in this file was taken with the extra boards present (#1808).

measurement_method.percentile_method: nearest-rank (no interpolation) over the 40 timed samples
measurement_method.auth: manage.py provision_fuzz_token --username demo2 (scoped, non-admin PAT; board_list alone authenticates as the board owner demo1 via --owner-token-file — same mechanism backend-schema-fuzz already uses)

budget_formula: budget_p95_ms = ceil(measured_p95_ms * 1.4 / 5) * 5 -- a 1.4x factor (issue #1082 specifies 1.3-1.5x) rounded up to the nearest 5ms so CI comparisons have a little headroom for measurement noise without the number itself being picked round. Recompute this whole file -- never hand-adjust a single budget_p95_ms -- when re-deriving.

board_list.note: Board list as the board OWNER (demo1, via --owner-token-file) so the access query spans the 20-member board; member_count/card_count/archived_card_count are independent correlated subqueries (#1723).

board_full.note: Serializes the entire board (all 2388 cards) in one response, unpaginated -- the most volume-sensitive endpoint in the fixture and the one this budget is least tolerant of relative headroom on, since a regression here is the one TruePPM's #2767 postmortem describes (index-shape regression, identical query count, higher latency). Also the most CPU-bound of the six (per-card DRF field serialization across ~2,388 cards, #1212), so it shows the most run-to-run variance on a shared CI runner -- expect wider swings here than on the lighter endpoints below.

card_search.note: The cross-board card query as a one-board user (demo2): access filter plus one 51-row cursor page. Card search now filters with the ci_contains lookup (ILIKE on PostgreSQL), which the pg_trgm GIN indexes from migration 0030 (card_title_trgm_idx / card_desc_trgm_idx) can serve for selective terms (#1809). This budget was measured before that change and is to be re-derived, and broad/short terms re-measured, in #2063. Derived after the #1805 fix (#1808). 'the' is a deliberately broad, high-cardinality search term -- it matches a large fraction of the corpus, closer to a real user's search-as-you-type behavior than a highly selective term would be.

card_search_multi_board.note: The same query as card_search, run as demo3, who can access 200 boards, so the card SELECT filters on a 200-id literal list. PostgreSQL is expected to scan the matching cards and sort instead of walking card_board_updated_idx (#1805 measured 13.5ms vs 0.65ms execution on the one-board fixture; this fixture layout was not EXPLAINed, so the plan is expected, not confirmed). Budget derived from a NUC run in #1808.

card_timeline.note: Unified movement + activity feed for a single card. Exercises the comment_card_created_idx / activity_card_created_idx composite indexes added in migration 0045.

card_list.note: Board card list, default 200-row cap with X-Total-Count/X-Truncated. Page read without a window count; a full page adds one bare COUNT (#2239).

cards_archived.note: First archived-cards page (50 rows). Page read without a window count; a full page adds one bare COUNT on the archived_at index (#2239).

notifications_list.note: The frontend polls this every 15-30s (visiban/settings.py's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES comment) -- the highest-QPS authenticated endpoint in the product, even though its own per-request cost is capped at 50 rows by NotificationListView.

notifications_unread.note: Companion to notifications_list -- polled at the same interval; unlike the list it is uncapped (counts all accessible unread rows).

board_summary.note: Per-swimlane counts plus a replay of the cards that entered a done column in the last 30 days (#448). Before #448 this was SQL aggregates only.

board_analytics.note: Heatmap, stalled cards and blocked time, with a replay of the cards relevant to the default 30-day window plus the frozen avg_days_per_column prefetch (#448).

flow_cycle_time.note: Replays every movement of the fixture board in Python (one query), then samples completions in the default 90-day range (#448).

flow_throughput.note: Same replay as flow_cycle_time, bucketed into whole ISO weeks (#448).

flow_cumulative_flow.note: Same replay; 90 days x columns from a difference array, never a per-day query (#448).

flow_wip_age.note: Same replay plus one query each for block rows and blocking relations (#448).
